CTE Pathway Equity Trends

Which student groups complete a Career Technical Education pathway at lower rates than the other students in their own school or district, how many more completers it would take to close that gap, and whether the gap is closing over time. Graduation cohorts 2019–2025 for every California district and charter school, with county and regional roll-ups.

How far each flagged group is from parity

How each group compares with its peers

"Lower than peers?" is Y when the group completed pathways at a lower rate than the other students in the same school or district, by both methods (disproportionate impact). Pooling five cohorts steadies small groups; the pooled span includes the pandemic-disrupted classes of 2021 and 2022.

How to read this

  • What is being compared. Every comparison is within one school, district, or roll-up: a student group is measured against the other students who graduated from the same place in the same year. A group is never compared with the state or with another district unless you choose a comparison in the filters.
  • Disproportionate impact means a group completed CTE pathways at a lower rate than its peers, by enough that it is unlikely to be chance. Two checks have to agree before a group is flagged.
  • Equity Index (EI) asks whether the group's share of pathway completers is as large as its share of the graduating class. If Hispanic students are 45% of graduates but 35% of completers, the index is about 0.78. Below 0.85 counts as a gap.
  • Percentage Point Gap minus one (PPG-1) asks whether the group's completion rate is below the rate of everyone else. "Minus one" means the group itself is left out of the comparison rate. A negative gap larger than the margin of error counts as a gap.
  • Y, Y*, Y**. Y means both checks agree. Y* means the same for a group of 30–50 students, and Y** for 10–29, where results are less certain. Groups under 10 students are not reported (*).
  • Parity means the group completes pathways at the same rate as its peers. Additional completers needed is how many more students from the group would have had to complete a pathway to get there. The two checks define the peer rate slightly differently, so each gives its own estimate; the lower and upper estimates are shown as a range.

Data notes

  • Source: California School Dashboard College/Career Indicator research files (cde.ca.gov/ta/ac/cm/ccidatafiles.asp). Pathway completion counts students meeting the CTE Pathway Completion criterion at the Prepared or Approaching Prepared level. 2021 and 2022 come from the Career Measures Only files released in the years without a Dashboard.
  • Pandemic-disrupted cohorts are the classes of 2020, 2021 and 2022. The class of 2020 lost the spring of senior year to the March 2020 closures; the class of 2021 spent most of senior year in distance learning; the class of 2022 returned to campus for senior year after a remote junior year. The class of 2023 is the first with junior and senior year fully in person.
  • District rows exclude charter schools, which appear as their own LEA. Region and county rows sum districts and charters; regions follow the California Community Colleges regional consortium map. Race/ethnicity groups are mutually exclusive; the other groups overlap. Long-Term English Learners (reported from 2023) are a subset of English Learners and are not shown separately.
  • This is a screening tool. It shows where a gap exists, not why. Small-group results should start a conversation, not settle one.
